archetype: A five-colour Dragon critical-mass deck with a verified extra-combat exit. deck-audit runs it as combo off strategic_frame.json, and the frame describes this exact 99: the sha prefixes differ (4a6369cc8929 against edc6644d0683) only because decklist.txt's hash covers the sideboard block that was retired, and deck-history reports no card delta after 47bb897. My disagreement with the frame is therefore substantive, not staleness. Its “the deck has no in-99 redundancy for the extra-combat effect” is too strong: grepping every oracle text in the 99 for an additional combat phase returns exactly two cards, Aggravated Assault and Scourge of the Throne. Scourge's costs no mana, but it triggers only on attacking the player with the most life and only once each turn — it hedges the effect without replacing the loop. The frame's conclusion, that Assault alone carries all three infinites, survives the correction; the premise under it does not.
verdict: The kill is real and certified: four of the six checker-passed stacks (001, 003, 004, 006) cover the deck's burst and its two Aggravated Assault loops. What limits it is mana. 34 lands against the 36-38 range, 16 of 34 entering tapped, and 28 nonland entries at mana value 5 or more, so the land drop hits 60.3% on turn 5 and 49.7% on turn 6 — the deck stalls exactly where it has to start deploying. Second, the engine it measures is not the engine it wins with: goldfish_targets.json declares six components and none of them contains Aggravated Assault.

cut_candidates.why: Mana value 8, and no discount reaches it. Enumerating all ten entries at mana value 7 or more — Ancient Gold Dragon, Drakuseth, Klauth, Old Gnawbone, Tiamat, Utvara Hellkite, Cavern-Hoard Dragon, Blasphemous Act, The Ur-Dragon, Dracogenesis — every one except Dracogenesis is either a Dragon creature spell (reachable by eminence, Urza's Incubator, Herald's Horn or Dragonspeaker Shaman) or reduces itself. Dracogenesis is an Enchantment that does neither, in a deck whose mean available mana is 4.937 on turn 6 and 6.539 on turn 10.
cut_candidates.cost_of_cutting: It is the deck's highest ceiling. Among the free-deployment effects in the 99 — Sneak Attack, Breaching Dragonstorm, Rishkar's Expertise, Hellkite Courser — it is the one that is both repeatable and keeps what it deploys: Sneak Attack sacrifices at the next end step, Hellkite Courser returns the commander at the next end step, and the other two are one free cast each. (The commander's own attack trigger does the same job better, but it is not in the 99 and it needs a nine-mana commander already on the battlefield.) Cutting this removes the turn where the deck simply empties its hand.

citations.quote: cut duplicated function before any uncovered class, and cut the ceiling card before the median one
Separate ceiling from median: the ceiling build runs one spectacular finisher and loses when it's answered; the median runs three cheap ones and closes from any board.

cut_candidates.why: Seven mana for a Dragon with flying and haste — it attacks and pays out the turn it resolves, so it never has to survive a turn cycle — but the mana it makes is restricted: “Spend this mana only to cast spells.” An activated ability is not a spell, so Klauth's mana cannot pay Aggravated Assault's {3}{R}{R}, Lathliss's {1}{R}, Scourge of Valkas's {R} firebreathing or Sneak Attack's {R}. mana_analysis.json never names Klauth at all — its assumptions say a source “counts only for mana it produces unconditionally; restricted mana (‘spend this mana only…’) counts for nothing (the deck-builder's rule)”, which is why it is absent from sources.producers. The enumeration of the deck's five spells-only Dragon sources — “Haven, Klauth, Maelstrom, Rivaz, Unclaimed Territory” — is in considering.json, not there. It accelerates the deck toward its plan and then cannot pay for the turn the plan wins.
cut_candidates.cost_of_cutting: Real and immediate. Flying and haste mean the payback needs no turn cycle: it attacks the turn it resolves and adds mana equal to the total power of attacking creatures, which on a Dragon board is a double-digit burst — enough to chain two haymaker Dragon spells in one turn, and Dragon spells are exactly what the restricted mana may be spent on. It is also a 4/4 flying Dragon body for the per-Dragon payoffs and for the commander's draw trigger.

cut_candidates.why: {3}{B}{B} in a deck with 16 black sources, where mana_analysis puts the on-curve black probability at 0.446 even counting rocks and dorks. It is also symmetric: every opponent names a type and rebuilds too, and interaction-breadth reports graveyard as the one uncovered class, so the deck cannot pre-empt what it hands back.
cut_candidates.cost_of_cutting: It is the deck's only MASS recursion — Haven of the Spirit Dragon returns one Dragon card to hand and Rivaz of the Claw casts one Dragon creature spell from the graveyard per turn. After a wrath it is the fastest route from an empty board to a lethal one: the whole Dragon graveyard returns at once and every per-Dragon payoff triggers on the way in.

cut_candidates.why: Six mana at {4}{B}{R} for a 6/5 flier whose text is mostly redundant here: Temur Ascendancy already gives the whole board haste and Dragon Tempest hastes every flier that enters, while Sneak Attack and Hellkite Courser haste what they deploy. The 10-life clause needs an opponent to cast a spell sharing a name with a card in their own graveyard, which almost never happens. It is also the most fragile of the three: Temur Ascendancy and Dragon Tempest are Enchantments and Crux of Fate destroys creatures only, so both survive either of its modes and both survive Blasphemous Act's 13 damage; a 6/5 Dragon survives neither Crux's Dragon mode nor the Act.
cut_candidates.cost_of_cutting: This is one of only two cards the taxonomy counts toward threat-density — the other is Boros Charm — and cutting it takes that axis from 2 to 1 against a floor of 3. It is also one of the deck's 22 Dragon creatures, so it raises X on Dragon Tempest and Scourge of Valkas, whose damage counts the Dragons you control, and it is one more card off the commander's attack trigger. Of the two effects that grant haste to the whole board it is the one that is not an Enchantment, so cutting it leaves that function answerable by a single enchantment sweeper.

gaps: strategic_frame.json's “the deck has no in-99 redundancy for the extra-combat effect” does not survive enumeration: Scourge of the Throne grants an additional combat, just not a repeatable one. That is a disagreement on the merits, not a staleness artifact — the frame's 4a6369cc8929 and the current edc6644d0683 differ only by the deleted sideboard block, so a strategic-frame refresh would rerun on a byte-identical 99 and settle nothing. What I cannot ground is whether one conditional, once-per-turn extra combat is worth anything as a hedge on the turn Assault is answered. Declaring an extra-combat component in goldfish_targets.json (open_questions[2]) would price it.

No deck_recon.json exists (deck-audit freshness reports recon absent), so this diagnosis leans on no meta evidence at all. Nothing here rests on what other Ur-Dragon lists run, and the 'is 34 lands normal for this commander' question is unanswered.

goldfish_metrics.json states 'Cost reducers, rituals, and extra card draw are not modeled (conservative)'. Every figure I quote from it — mean_cast_turn 8.967, mean_available_mana_by_turn, mean_bodies_by_turn — is therefore a floor for a deck whose first declared engine component is cost reduction. A goldfish that modelled reduction would resize the mana finding.

card_roles.json classifies 93.7% of this deck and has no pattern for six cards: Aggravated Assault, Chaos Warp, Dracogenesis, Patriarch's Bidding, Rishkar's Expertise, Sneak Attack. The combo plan routes through the first of those, which is why the ramp, sweepers, threat-density and interaction counts all read low.

findings.note: Re-ran `deck-audit ur-dragon` fresh. All 16 measured.value figures match exactly (34 / 46 / 5 / -20 / 20 / 4 / 11 / 1 / 6 / 2 / 24 / 4 / 0.883 / 3 / 4 / 7). Every reading agrees with its own value: I re-derived 28 nonland entries at MV>=5, 5 at MV8+, 66 nonland entries, 9 basics, 34 land copies / 29 entries, R at 47 of 101 pips with 32 red cards, B at 6 cards, on_curve B with rocks/dorks 0.446, keep rate 0.751, land-drop 0.883/0.603/0.497 at t3/t5/t6, mean available mana 4.937 t6 and 6.539 t10, mean_bodies 1.463 t6, commander mean_cast_turn 8.967 with cast_by_turn_6 0.0. mana_analysis.json and goldfish_metrics.json are both freshness-current against decklist sha edc6644d0683; bracket-check re-run today still returns floor 4 with the same three Game Changers and three two-card infinites.

The three axes where the diagnosis departs from the audit verdict all engage the audit's own probe/floor notes rather than dodging them. ramp: OVER at 20 is rebutted by an enumeration whose 20 names match the audit's list card-for-card, and the 12 residual accelerants are all MV<=3 (verified against cards.json cmc). card-advantage: the audit probe names 5 uncounted cards; the diagnosis engages 3 of them and adds Tiamat, Breaching Dragonstorm, Korlessa, Herald's Horn and the commander's attack trigger, all confirmed in oracle text, and hedges 'most of it is board-dependent'. threat-density: ADEQUATE at 2 against a floor of 3 rests on stacks 001/003/004/006, and I confirmed all six stacks in stacks/ carry checker.verdict == pass with the titles the diagnosis attributes to them.

The staleness framing is gone and the replacement argument is verifiable end to end. `git show 47bb897:data/decks/ur-dragon/decklist.txt | shasum -a 256` is 4a6369cc8929 (== strategic_frame.json's decklist_sha256_prefix) and the working file is edc6644d0683; `git diff 47bb897 5371a4a -- decklist.txt` removes ONLY the 38-line Sideboard block, and `deck-history` shows no card delta after 47bb897. The frame therefore describes this exact 99. The merits disagreement also holds: regexing all 95 entries' oracle_text for an additional combat phase returns exactly two cards, Aggravated Assault and Scourge of the Throne, and Scourge's text is 'attacks for the first time each turn, if it's attacking the player with the most life', so once-per-turn and conditional is accurate. The frame quote 'the deck has no in-99 redundancy for the extra-combat effect' is verbatim in strategic_frame.json key_tensions.

I re-ran both functions rather than accepting the report. deck_audit._interaction_breadth over cards.json plus a Bojuka Bog entry returns graveyard: 0 and 4 classes covered, identical to the base run — card_roles.json gives Bojuka Bog only ['land:tapped'] and the function gates on SUITE_ROLES, so the entry's claim that a post-swap audit still reports graveyard uncovered is exactly right. mana_analysis.analyze with the Bog added returns lands.total 34->35, B sources 16->17 against a 36 target (worst-colour -20 -> -19), enters_tapped 16->17, and the unconditional tapland count 5->6. Every figure in the entry matches. `closes: mana-base` is legitimate under the doctor charter's semantics ('closes a named axis'), the entry discloses that 35 is still under the 36-38 band, and it does not claim the graveyard class as the axis it closes.

The pass-2 defect is genuinely gone, not annotated. Klauth is a 4/4 with 'Flying, haste' (cards.json), so the payback needs no turn cycle, and both `why` and `cost_of_cutting` now say so. The restriction claim holds: 'Spend this mana only to cast spells', so it cannot pay Aggravated Assault's {3}{R}{R}, Lathliss's {1}{R}, Scourge of Valkas's {R} or Sneak Attack's {R} — all four are activated abilities in the deck's own oracle text. mana_analysis.json's sources.producers list does not contain Klauth, and the assumption quoted about restricted mana is verbatim. The 'five spells-only Dragon sources' enumeration is verbatim in considering.json as attributed.

The self-damage disclosure is now correct and complete, and my pass-2 note is corrected as instructed. cards.json gives exactly two non-Dragon creatures — Dragonspeaker Shaman 2/2 and Rivaz of the Claw 3/3 (Legendary Creature — Lizard Warlock) — and both die to Dragonback Assault's 3 damage. Korlessa, Scale Singer is 1/4 and IS a Dragon Bard, so it survives; the minimum toughness across all 22 Dragon entries is 4 (Korlessa 1/4, Thrakkus 3/4), so 'all survive it' holds. Dragonspeaker Shaman is in engine.components[0] and Rivaz in components[2], so 'two components rather than one' is right.
